steps.content: Beep, beep, beep... A rhythmic electronic pulse underscores your work, an ouroboros of sound looping endlessly as you flip through documents. In the corner of your screen, notifications bloom and vanish in a silent, frantic dance.
Wynn stands by your desk, her eyes flicking toward the chiming terminal. She tries to contain her curiosity, but the relentless beeping wears her resolve thin.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief, those alerts are so... rhythmic. And they're not stopping at all. Are you sure it's okay to just ignore them?
They're just periodic updates from Ceto's tracker. Basic telemetry and a visual feed. The system will flag any Mania fluctuations or unusual movement automatically.
Your attention drops back to the report on the Rancors and lighthouse keepers. Wynn, however, remains captivated by the slideshow of images auto-advancing on the screen.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: It's so... still. Is it lagging? Or is nothing really happening? Oh, wait, there she goes! Chief, even without sound, you can see a whole story in this!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: It's like a flipbook! Way more interesting than a live feed. It kind of feels like... you're following along on someone's trip!

Following along on someone's trip... The phrase pulls your gaze to the screen. The footage is choppy, a silent film stripped of context, yet you can still trace the narrative woven through its distinct scenes—the shifting backdrops, the subtle changes in posture, the quiet emotions flowing from one frame to the next.

Wynn's comment echoes the fragments you have collected over these past few days: a silent, stuttering reel of "Ceto's DisCity tour." It is a catalog of moments that have, more than once, offered a fleeting respite from the tension of the looming war.

After Ceto's Departure
　　00:27:43

On screen, Ceto holds the girl's hand, her gaze intense as she studies the features of the towering buildings. Eastside is a steel forest of identical residential complexes, and this one appears utterly unremarkable.
So, this is her first destination? Her sense of direction seems to work perfectly well in DisCity. Not bad, she's making good progress.

After Ceto's Departure
　　00:35:29

When you look at the screen again, the scene is a near-perfect replica of the last: Ceto stands before what seems to be the same cluster of buildings, her posture unchanged. The only difference is the faint trace of uncertainty now clouding her expression.
This can't be the same complex... can it?

A check of the coordinates confirms she has traveled a significant distance. The architecture is just unnervingly identical. Now on alert, Ceto shifts, positioning the girl protectively behind her as if expecting the maze of towers to launch an ambush.

After Ceto's Departure
　　00:43:37
How did she end up back here again... No, wait. It looks like the same complex from before, but a different entrance...

Without a detailed map, Ceto remains unaware of this. She stares at the familiar signage, her furrowed brow and tense expression suggesting she's contemplating the most efficient way to reduce it to rubble. A semicircle of onlookers has gathered at a distance, pointing and whispering.
In the footage, a security guard emerges from his post in the bottom left corner. Simultaneously, the girl notices the development and hesitantly reaches for the hem of Ceto's clothing.

After Ceto's Departure
　　00:45:13
You know the routine notifications mean intervention isn't required. But after witnessing this series of events, focusing on data reports becomes impossible. Your eyes are drawn back to the screen.

The girl takes the initiative, grabbing Ceto's hand and pulling her away at the critical moment, evading the security guard's suspicious glare. Ceto's expression is pure bewilderment. She clearly doesn't understand the need for a tactical retreat, but she doesn't resist.

Your hand moves almost on its own, capturing this moment from across the city. The file preserves a rare, unprecedented expression on Ceto's face amidst the bustling crowd: a mix of bewilderment, dawning realization, and the faint, reluctant smile of someone who has just understood their mistake.

After Ceto's Departure
　　01:37:19

In the image, Ceto clutches her tracking device—a makeshift terminal—facing off against a security guard requesting a registration she doesn't understand. They are locked in a silent, hopelessly confused standoff, unsure whose and which code to scan. The flickering black-and-white pattern casts a shifting light over Ceto's tightly pressed lips.

The little girl watches, head tilted, observing the adults' clumsy, futile attempts to navigate the screen. Seeing no progress, she rises onto her tiptoes, a small hand reaching out to aid the two well-intentioned but utterly ineffective grown-ups.

After Ceto's Departure
　　02:56:40

The photo freezes Ceto standing like a grim quarantine barrier between the girl and a brightly dressed flyer promoter offering candy. The promoter is baffled by such intense vigilance, staring blankly at Ceto, whose entire posture radiates a wall of pure rejection.

Mirroring her protector, the little girl clutches the hem of Ceto's clothes, hiding behind her. Only her stern little face is visible, peeking out with an expression that uncannily echoes Ceto's own hardened glare.

After Ceto's Departure
　　04:02:33
It's true. Compared to a continuous video feed, these fragmented moments better convey a sense of progression, a journey viewed step by step.

You turn your head slightly. The timestamps keep advancing, and the narrative is now reaching its conclusion. The scene shows an apartment doorway. The camera's high angle, limited by its mount, frames Ceto's straight-backed silhouette against a glimpse of the interior.

A woman, her eyes glistening, clutches Ceto's hand, speaking with visible emotion. The little girl waits nearby, safe in her father's arms. Ceto's brief role as a protector is over; her back is once again unaccompanied, yet her posture seems more resolute than before.

You save the final photo. In it, Ceto is withdrawing her hand, having just pressed something into the girl's palm. The child stands in the doorway, now cradling a cellophane-wrapped candy, her face illuminated with a radiant joy.

The "Save Successful" notification flashes and vanishes, immediately replaced by an incoming call alert from Ceto's temporary terminal. You glance around and notice that Wynn has, at some point, quietly closed the door for you. You answer the call.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Mission's done. Took a little longer than I figured, but... it went smooth.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The family said they spent everything they had looking for her. If they'd given up hope, they'd have moved on by now.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: So... a few days later, and my skills and her memory might not have been enough. Not for a clean result like this.

You listen silently to her words—still terse, blunt, and somewhat stiff. Yet, though only a few hours have passed, the Ceto navigating the streets of Eastside is no longer a complete stranger to this city.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You made this happen. Thanks, ${PlayerName}.
I didn't do anything. Finding her, bringing her back to DisCity, getting her home... that was all you. Even the decision to protect her, from the start, was...
Suddenly, the street scene behind Ceto freezes. Something has snagged her attention, a rare occurrence for someone of her singular focus, halting your conversation mid-sentence.
Ceto?

Even at the sound of her name, her tense profile remains rigid, offering no acknowledgment, much less a return to your dialogue. So you change tactics. You abandon your questions and instead listen, straining to catch the faint trace of whatever sound has so completely captured her.

steps.speaker: Woman's Voice
steps.content: Do you really have to go, honey? Mrs. McKay says it's getting dangerous out there. The business is bad enough... but now people aren't even making it home safe. We still have some savings left. We can manage...

steps.speaker: Woman's Voice
steps.content: It's not much, but it's enough. You don't need to risk yourself... I'm so scared you won't come back. If something happens to you, what will Lily and I do? Have you even thought of that?

steps.speaker: Chief, Chief... What's wrong? Do you have low blood pressure? Here, have some chocolate!
steps.content: ...Of course I have, honey. I've thought about who'd protect you if I were gone... But I still have to go. No, it's because of that, I have to go!

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: A storm is coming. I can't just sit here and watch our savings run out. You know how it is. The worse things get, the more we need to fall back on. I need to protect you both. That's why I have to go. That's my fight!

The voices are faint, nearly swallowed by the din of the city. You would have to strain to catch them. But for a Sinner like Ceto, they are likely as clear as if they were being spoken right beside her.

For one such as her, she can undoubtedly discern the subtle tremor in the woman's voice, the thread of resolve woven through the man's, and the sharp edge of mockery in the whispers of passersby. And beneath it all, she may hear something more: the relentless undercurrent of this era that flows just beneath their words.

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: Daddy... are you going far? Here, this is for you. The teacher says when mommies and daddies go far away, good children give them their favorite things. Then you won't cry until your eyes get ouchie from missing me.

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: But... this is your favorite candy. My Lily is... so thoughtful, worrying her daddy will cry... Ahem...

steps.speaker: Child's Voice
steps.content: Are you crying now, Daddy? Don't cry, your eyes will get all hurty... Eat the candy! It'll make your eyes better!

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: No, Daddy won't eat it... I'll keep it right here. For when I miss you and Mommy so much it hurts, then I'll eat it. Lily, remember: no matter how far I am, I'll always be thinking of you. Always protecting you.

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: Be good for Mommy. I promise I'll do everything I can to come back to you. Quickly!

The conversation has ended, the family has left, yet Ceto remains, anchored in place. Her eyes narrow slightly, as if gazing at a distant, brilliant glare, perhaps the way sunlight catches on cellophane. Her profile is still, weathered and unchanging as a reef stone shaped by coastal winds.
What do you see now?

Silence stretches, but as Ceto resumes walking, the tapestry of DisCity's streets unfolding behind her once again, you can almost feel the gears turning in her mind. She isn't refusing to answer; she is assembling her thoughts. And when she finally speaks, her voice is decisive.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I saw what you, Fynn, and the others talked about. "Something worth protecting." And... "a reason to fight."
Is that what you were hoping to see? Has DisCity... given you the answers you were looking for?

This time, there is no hesitation. She lifts her gaze, looking squarely into the monitoring device as if seeing through it, across the distance, directly to you—the person who once described DisCity to her from within the lighthouse.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Yes. I have my answer now.

Behind her, the city pulses: a flow of rushing crowds, the rhythm of blinking neon, the living, breathing entity of a metropolis and its people. With the ghost of her comrades' homeland at her back, Ceto now strides forward, her path clear, moving toward the city gates, toward the end of the promise you secured for her.
...Maybe we'll meet again soon. When we do, Ceto, I hope you've found a place to call your own. And something worth protecting.
Whatever that place is. Whatever that something turns out to be.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: It's not about worth, Ceto. We fight to protect our families back in DisCity. But you... you have no one there to protect.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Standing guard here is tough. These blades take a piece of you. But it's worth it to keep our families safe. For you, it's just pure sacrifice. Nothing in return. What's the point?

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: In the heat of battle, there's no time to think... Ah, forget I said anything, Ceto. Don't take an old man's worries to heart. It's just... you're my daughter's age. Kids your age should have candy in their mouths and a grin on their faces, not weapons in their hands.

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: A storm is coming. I can't just sit here and watch our savings run out. You know how it is. The worse things get, the more we need to fall back on. I need to protect you both. That's why I have to go. That's my fight!

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: No, Daddy won't eat it... I'll keep it right here. For when I miss you and Mommy so much it hurts, then I'll eat it. Lily, remember: no matter how far I am, I'll always be thinking of you. Always protecting you.

steps.speaker: Man's Voice
steps.content: Be good for Mommy. I promise I'll do everything I can to come back to you. Quickly!

A young father, a tearful mother, a child clinging to her mother's leg, her small face confused by the grief of a parting she cannot understand. These are the moments treasured like candies, carefully preserved in their shimmering wrappers.

Is this what Fynn and Herbert sought to protect? When Herbert left this city for the outpost—the lighthouse before the Black Tide, where Ceto met him—had he, too, carried the memory of a scene like this?
What are you looking at? What do you see now?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I saw... a different kind of lighthouse keepers. No special weapons. No combat training. Not even a soldier's resolve. Just the most ordinary people.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Family? DisCity? It's all temporary... Even without a Rancor's voice in their heads, the battlefield will still break them. That hell will swallow them whole and spit out monsters!
She closes her eyes, clenching her fists.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: But I'm not like them. I'm a Sinner. I crawled out of the Black Tide. That cursed blade lost its hold on me long ago.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm stronger, much stronger than those ordinary people. I can fight to the last breath. I can kill the things they can't. I can protect what I decide to protect.
Even if she cannot prevent tragedies like what befell the lighthouse keepers from ever happening again, she can still fight to ensure they happen less often.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I know where I have to go. Back to that hell, the battlefield. I was born in it, forged by it. It's only right that I'm the one to wipe it from the earth. End it once and for all.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: For everyone, past or future, who just wants to go home... Let my life be the price! Let them have a home to return to. That... is what I will protect!

Ceto opens her eyes. The battlefield stretches before her; the weight of her weapon rests solidly in her hand. This world is one of sharp, unforgiving edges, a pressure that should be suffocating. Yet she finds it comforting. Familiar. It is a reality she can command.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: One.

She kills the monster before her and takes a step forward. The act no longer feels like sinking into a hollow, bottomless swamp. Now, each kill delivers a clear, tangible feedback—a purpose solid enough to count, one by one.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Two.

Another creature falls with a dying howl as other Rancor soldiers carve a path through her flanks. She presses onward. Here, killing is survival. Fighting is survival. And for the first time, both survival and combat hold meaning.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Three.

Forward. Always forward. The soldiers form a living barrier against the endless surge of monsters, like the cliff face once battered by the Black Tide. This battlefield is far from DisCity, but she knows with absolute clarity what lies behind this defense line.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The more I kill... the longer I hold... the more I can protect. Fynn, Herbert... ${PlayerName}. Is this what you all believed in?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...Ha. So this is what it feels like... to fight for something worth protecting.
Perhaps she has finally found it: a homeland, a place of belonging. Her new "lighthouse."
